page: Vultr vc2-4c-8gb is a Cloud Compute instance featuring 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with 2 threads per core using the x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 8.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance's processing capabilities in the lower tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench register in the bottom 10% to 25% categories. Memory performance shows a stark contrast between cached and uncached operations; small-block cached read bandwidth achieves an average tier result of 367.64 GB/sec, whereas large-block uncached read and write speeds drop to the bottom 25% at 24.41 GB/sec and 19.55 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET performance also rank in the bottom 10% tier.

Due to the shared CPU allocation, this instance presents a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The primary tradeoff is the potential for resource contention and lower overall processing throughput, as reflected in the weak benchmark scores. This resource profile is appropriate for lightweight web serving, basic software compilation, development environments, and low-throughput utility tasks rather than intensive database or real-time processing workloads.
